title: Count Occurrences Using Binary Search
statement:
Given a sorted array of N integers (may contain duplicates) and a target T, count how many times T appears in the array.

Use lower_bound and upper_bound (both implemented with binary search) so the total complexity is O(log N).

Count = upper_bound(T) - lower_bound(T).
constraints:
1 <= N <= 10^7
-10^9 <= A[i] <= 10^9
Array is in non-decreasing order.
-10^9 <= T <= 10^9
inputFormat:
Line 1: two integers N and T.
Line 2: N space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.
outputFormat: A single integer: the number of times T appears.

examples.explanation: 5 appears at indices 4 and 5. Count = upper_bound - lower_bound = 6 - 4 = 2.
